verdict: Cencora grew revenue 5.5% to $88.4B and swung back to a $519M profit for shareholders, because gross profit jumped 22% while the big one-off charges that hit a year ago did not repeat.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs -$1.75 a year ago — net income attributable to Cencora was $519M

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +21% YoY — excludes deal, legal and similar one-off items

segments.name: U.S. Healthcare Solutions
segments.note: Delivering medicines and health products to hospitals, doctors and pharmacies in the US. Up 5.4% on overall market growth, more specialty products and more GLP-1 diabetes and weight-loss drugs, plus the OneOncology business bought in February 2026. Segment operating income was $998M, up 22%.

segments.name: International Healthcare Solutions
segments.note: The same work outside the US, including Canada and global specialty logistics (shipping delicate medicines worldwide). Up 5.1% as reported, and up 7.8% ignoring currency moves. Segment operating income was $152M, up 16%.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Profarma (Brazil), MWI Animal Health (vet supplies) and consulting businesses. Cencora reports this group at $2,302M; it is shown here at $2,266M after removing $37M of sales between Cencora's own segments, plus a $1M rounding adjustment, so the segments sum exactly to total revenue. Segment operating income was $101M, up 36%.

opex.name: Distribution, selling, and administrative
opex.note: Warehouses, delivery trucks, sales teams and the back office. Up 24% YoY, mainly because the OneOncology deal (February 2026) added a whole business. Shown $1M above the reported $2,173M so the rounded lines tie — see the footer note.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, equipment and bought intangible assets (customer lists and similar) over their useful lives. Includes $116M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles.

opex.name: Litigation & opioid
opex.note: Litigation and opioid-related expenses — legal costs and charges tied to opioid lawsuits and other litigation — treated by Cencora as one-off items.

opex.name: Deal & integration costs
opex.note: Acquisition and divestiture-related deal and integration expenses — costs of buying and selling businesses and combining them, including $94M of adjustments to equity units from the RCA and OneOncology deals.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring and other expenses — costs of reorganizing parts of the business — treated by Cencora as one-off items.

otherDetail: Other expense was $120M, net: $136M of interest expense, net, partly offset by $17M of other income, net. (The exact net was $119.6M, which rounds to $120M.)

takeaways.title: Sales grew in every business
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5.5% to $88.4B. US sales grew 5.4% to $78.3B, international sales grew 5.1% to $7.8B, and the smaller Other businesses grew 10.1% to $2.3B. Growth came from more units sold, including specialty products and GLP-1 medicines.

takeaways.title: Each sale kept a little more
takeaways.text: Gross profit jumped 22% to $3.6B, and gross margin widened from 3.53% to 4.08% of revenue. The OneOncology acquisition lifted US margins, partly offset by fast-growing GLP-1 drugs, which carry thinner margins. For a distributor that keeps only about 4 cents of each sales dollar before running costs, that shift is large.

takeaways.title: Back to profit after a one-off-heavy year-ago quarter
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Cencora was $519M, versus a $340M loss a year ago, when a $724M goodwill impairment on PharmaLex crushed the quarter. Leaving out one-offs, adjusted EPS was $4.66, up 21% — the clearest sign the underlying business improved.

oneTimers: Acquisition and divestiture-related deal and integration costs were $177M in the quarter, including $94M of adjustments to RCA and OneOncology equity units and a $17M increase in the expected purchase price for RCA (contingent consideration — extra payment if the business performs).
Restructuring and other expenses were $65M and litigation and opioid-related expenses were $12M. Cencora treats both as one-off items outside its adjusted results.

Gross profit included two one-off boosts: a $38M gain from antitrust litigation settlements and a $6M LIFO credit (an inventory-accounting adjustment), partly offset by $15M of currency remeasurement expense in Türkiye.
footerNote: Reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M. Distribution, selling and administrative is shown at $2,174M (reported $2,173M) so the rounded lines tie.
